chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Ibn Abi Ya'fur asked him, 'How many rak'at should I pray?' He said, 'Pray eight rak'at at the time of the sun's declination (Dhuhr), for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Prayer in my mosque is like a thousand [prayers] in other mosques, except for the Sacred Mosque, for prayer in the Sacred Mosque equals a thousand prayers in my mosque.'

key_terms.زَوَالِ اَلشَّمْسِ: Declination of the sun (time for Dhuhr prayer)
key_terms.مَسْجِدِي: My mosque (referring to the Prophet's mosque in Medina)

ai.seo_question: How many rak'at are prescribed for the Dhuhr prayer according to this hadith, and what is the reward for praying in the Prophet's mosque?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the preferred method of performing Dhuhr by combining the four obligatory rak'at with four voluntary ones, totaling eight, to be offered at the time of the sun's declination. The hadith further elucidates the hierarchical virtue of prayer locations, establishing that while the Prophet's Mosque (Masjid al-Nabawi) offers a reward equivalent to a thousand prayers elsewhere, the Sacred Mosque (Masjid al-Haram) surpasses this with a reward of one thousand prayers relative to the Prophet's Mosque, thereby emphasizing the unique sanctity of the two holiest sites in Shia jurisprudence.
